Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Underwriting Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Investment Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; Emily Davis, Chief Claims Officer; and Alex Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to David Johnson.

David Johnson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust policy retention rates across major product lines, a fortified capital position with elevated statutory surplus levels, prudent changes in actuarial assumptions, substantial reinsurance recoveries both received and anticipated, solid gross written premiums growth by line of business, favorable realized and unrealized gains and losses on investments, manageable total catastrophe losses relative to gross written premiums, and a well-diversified asset allocation overview encompassing fixed income, equities, and alternatives. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Sarah, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $500 million, or $2.10 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included enhanced policy retention, capital strength, actuarial refinements, reinsurance support, premium expansion, investment returns, catastrophe management, and portfolio diversification. Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $650 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with 458% risk-based capital. Our expense ratio also improved to 28.5%.

Let me dive deeper into these elements, starting with policy retention rates by major product line, a cornerstone of our profitability that directly boosts lifetime value per policyholder, cuts customer acquisition costs estimated at 20-25% of first-year premiums, and ensures stable premium revenue even in choppy markets. Our company-wide retention rate stood firm at 89.2% in Q3, up 110 basis points year-over-year and achieving our 11th straight quarter of sequential gains, surpassing the industry composite of 87.5% for large diversified carriers as per AM Best.

By major lines, personal lines—auto and homeowners, making up 61% of our in-force book at $14.2 billion annualized premium—saw personal auto retention climb to 87.5%, gaining 150 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 220 basis points year-over-year. This resilience persists despite repair cost inflation up 8.2% year-over-year per Mitchell benchmarks and higher claims frequency from distracted driving, issues noted by peers like Progressive. Our advantage stems from the ApexDrive telematics program, embraced by 42% of auto policyholders, leveraging AI for usage-based insurance that personalizes premiums and yields 15% lower lapse rates via 12-18% average discounts. We've added behavioral prompts through our mobile app, slashing mid-term cancellations by 9%.

Homeowners retention reached a record 92.3%, up 80 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 190 basis points year-over-year. Even with catastrophe losses from Hurricane Helene and California wildfires totaling $450 million net—mirroring Travelers' experience—our proactive measures shone. Climate-resilient underwriting models using Verisk's wildfire risk scores prompted non-renewals on 7% of our California book to safeguard margins. Bundling auto and home achieved 68% penetration, lifting retention 250 basis points for bundled customers via loyalty perks. U.S. personal retention averaged 89.8%, while UK personal lines rose to 91.2% with FCA-compliant pricing transparency tools.

Commercial lines—property & casualty and workers' comp, 28% of the book at $6.8 billion annualized—posted commercial P&C retention at 88.7%, up 120 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 160 year-over-year, bucking a softening rate cycle with flat-to-down pricing in middle-market renewals per McKinsey's Q3 analysis. Our mid-market emphasis—policies from $50K to $5M—thrives on account-based servicing through the EagleEye portal, offering brokers real-time loss runs and endorsements, cutting voluntary lapses 11%. Workers' comp retention hit 90.1%, up 200 basis points year-over-year, powered by Return-to-Work programs that shortened claim durations 14% through Teladoc telemedicine ties. North American commercial averaged 89.5%, though EMEA post our 2023 UK specialty broker acquisition trailed at 86.2% from Brexit supply chain issues inflating liability claims; we're addressing this with fleet telematics aiming for 88%+ by year-end.

Life & annuity, 8% of the book at $1.9 billion annualized, saw life persistency at 94.6% on a 13th-month basis, up 90 basis points year-over-year above LIMRA's 92.1% average. Term life led at 95.2% via no-exam underwriting with Milliman predictive analytics, cutting issue times below 48 hours. Annuity retention stayed at 97.8%, aided by fixed indexed products yielding 5.2% amid Fed rate cuts, beating Allianz benchmarks. In Asia-Pacific, 22% of life premiums via joint ventures, retention eased to 93.1% from China surrender value regulations, but WeChat mini-apps steadied digital servicing.

Group health & specialty, 3% at $0.7 billion, improved group health to 91.4%, up 140 basis points year-over-year, as stop-loss renewals gained from value-based care pilots with UnitedHealthcare networks trimming large claims 16%. Specialty like cyber and D&O held at 89.9%, steady despite ransomware creep akin to Beazley.

These gains reflect our Retention-First framework: 82% digital self-service via app and portal, AI churn models catching 65% at-risk policies for outreach, and ESG incentives like green home discounts for LEED certifications. Our $150 million 2024 tech spend here yields 3:1 ROI by curbing acquisition costs. We guide full-year company-wide retention to 89.5-90.0%, personal lines to 90%+ with telematics at 50% penetration. While inflation risks linger, our 88.2% ex-cat combined ratio fortifies us, outpacing Allstate's 86.9% personal and Chubb's 87.8% commercial via our data edge.

Shifting to our capital position and statutory surplus levels, vital for weathering catastrophes, fueling growth, and shareholder returns under statutory accounting principles amid NAIC and Solvency II oversight. At quarter-end, our consolidated RBC ratio was a sturdy 458%, exceeding our 400-450% target and NAIC's 200% action level, up 12 points sequentially from 446% and 22 points year-over-year from 436%. Statutory surplus closed at $15.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year from $14.1 billion and 3% sequentially, growing faster than earned premiums by 200 basis points despite loss pressures. P&C surplus reached $10.8 billion, up 10% year-over-year; L&H at $4.4 billion, up 4% on annuity sales and crediting rates.

Drivers included stellar investments with a 4.8% statutory book yield from the higher-for-longer Fed stance. Fixed income at 72% locked yields on investment-grade corporates and munis averaging 5.2%, trimming duration to 5.8 years from 6.2 for volatility protection amid Treasury shifts. Equities at 12% added gains from S&P 500's 15% YTD rise, though trimmed post-April rally for a 65/35 fixed-to-alternative tilt.

Underwriting contributed via a 92.4% P&C combined ratio, $450 million favorable prior-year development in workers' comp and auto liability, and $320 million pre-tax cat losses below seasonal norms despite Helene, thanks to reinsurance ceding 45% of U.S. P&C above $500 million retention via quota-share with Swiss Re and Munich Re, plus $1.2 billion collateralized from our Bermuda captive at 22% blended commission.

Regionally, U.S. Southeast P&C surplus grew 12% to $4.1 billion, absorbing $180 million Helene hits lighter than Travelers or Chubb due to 9.2% Florida homeowners rate gains. Europe Lloyd's syndicate surplus rose 15% to £850 million on specialty casualty amid Ukraine disruptions. Asia-Pacific up 6% to $1.1 billion via India microinsurance JVs with HDFC Ergo.

Strategically, a $750 million share repurchase authorized with $220 million deployed in-quarter at 8% below book value aids EPS. Quarterly dividends hold at $0.85 per share, 55% payout. $1.5 billion earmarked for M&A in cyber and ESG parametric triggers, pricing $300 million new business at 25% margins. $150 million in AI cat modeling with RMS and AIR cut tail VaR 18% in ORSA tests; economic capital now TCFD-aligned, surplus solid through 2028 even in 1-in-250-year hurricanes. Multi-year reinsurance shaved costs to 12.5% of premiums.

We project year-end RBC above 460%, surplus over $16 billion on normalized cats and 4.5% yields.

Next, changes in actuarial assumptions and their impacts, key to reserve dynamics especially for long-duration products like universal life with secondary guarantees, indexed universal life, and fixed indexed annuities. Assumptions cover mortality, morbidity, lapses, persistency, discount rates, and expenses, updated annually or on new evidence under US GAAP. This quarter, net unfavorable $120 million pre-tax from updates—8 basis points to operating ROE—mainly in individual life and retirement, versus $45 million favorable last year post-pandemic boosts.

Longevity and mortality drove $85 million unfavorable: credibility-weighted studies on 1.2 million policies showed post-COVID improvements for ages 65-80 in term and whole life, aligning to 2023 Valuation Basic Table from Society of Actuaries like Prudential and Lincoln National. This extended modal expectancies 2-3 years on $15 billion liabilities. North America took 95%, hitting Medicare Supplement and LTCI; Europe milder at €20 million under IFRS 17 CSM for UK pension risk transfers with Legal & General; Asia negligible on shorter par products.

Lapses and persistency offset favorably $40 million: FIA and IUL surrenders at 9.5% annualized vs. prior 8.2% amid 5.25-5.50% Fed funds, per LIMRA 15% YoY spike. Refined ULSG anti-selection cut persistency 1.5 points. Retirement released $30 million from $25 billion FIA; Latin America neutral on bancassurance with Itaú Unibanco.

Discount rates added $50 million unfavorable, 25 basis point drop on 4.1% 10-year Treasury for VAs with living benefits on $10 billion separate accounts, like Athene. Net spread held at 105 basis points on $180 billion portfolio's 4.8% yield from RMBS and ILBs; macrohedging with futures and swaps cut VA GMxB $15 million.

Expenses and morbidity netted favorable $25 million: 4% better disability morbidity post-Omicron released $20 million; 2% tighter expenses on automation offset 3.2% medical CPI.

Net: individual life -$70 million, retirement -$30 million, group/specialty +$5 million. YTD net unfavorable $200 million, yet reserves up 7% to $145 billion at low 220% RBC above 400-450% target.

Our Actuarial Modernization Platform on Google Cloud Vertex AI and Prophet handled 50 terabytes claims data, boosting credibility 30% with ML GLMs. Ahead on IFRS 17 for Bermuda sub at 95% CSM. New business margins up 50 basis points to 12.5% on dynamic IUL lapses. Expect neutral-to-favorable 2024 from CDC mortality normalization and rate cuts hitting peers harder on our 60/40 public/private mix. Minimal climate bleed.

On reinsurance recoveries received and expected, crucial mitigant to gross losses amid cats. Our P&C—72% GWP—benefits from quota share, XoL, cat aggregate with Swiss Re, Munich Re, RenaissanceRe, Berkshire.

YTD received $1.47 billion, up 28% YoY from $1.15 billion, 92% billings in 45 days. Cats $1.12 billion (76%): $450 million Fiona net reinstatement, 65% ceded on 1-in-100 PML to $2.5 billion; $380 million Idalia via ILW at $15 billion industry loss on RMS v18.1. Non-cat large $250 million, e.g., $120 million California wildfire 50/50 with PartnerRe. L&H $100 million on longevity/mortality swaps with Hannover Re.

Regions: North America 68% ($1.0 billion) US cats; EMEA 18% ($265 million) floods; APAC 14% ($205 million) Typhoon Mawar. Recoveries 68% gross incurred vs. 62% prior, on 4.5% ROL hikes at January renewal.

Expected additional $2.1-2.4 billion over 18 months, $1.3 billion Q4/H1 2024: $1.6 billion Idalia/California rivers pending assessments, AIR 10-15% upside; $400-500 million aggregate 82% eroded; $300 million run-off. 10% adverse development -$200 million risk, but 95% collateral.

Analytics: Verisk Touchstone ML cut PML uncertainty 18%, laddering quota 40% then five XoL to $10 billion. Panel diversified, single exposure down to 14%, ILS cat bonds $300 million at 7.2%. 1/1/2024 2-3% ROL, collars/loss caps for La Niña. APAC 55% typhoon ceded; EMEA cyber $80 million YTD.

Recoveries compressed combined to 92.4% ex-cat (95.8% all-lines) vs. 97.2% guide, +$450 million earnings; ceded loss ratio 42% on $2.8 billion ceded premiums up 12%, ROE 14.5%.

Gross written premiums grew 9.2% year-over-year to $14.8 billion, strongest in three years on pricing, 88.5% retention, selective expansion; organic 10.1% ex-FX.

Personal lines 42% at $6.2 billion, up 7.8%: auto 6.2% on 4.5% rates despite 12% repair inflation, ApexDrive 2.1 million users cut loss ratios 15%; homeowners/dwellings 12.4% on 8-10% hikes Florida/California offsetting $450 million cats, $300 million parametric with Swiss Re at 92% combined.

Commercial 28% $4.1 billion up 14.6% on 11.2% rates: property 16.2% logistics/manufacturing; workers' comp 13.8% payroll/services, AI underwriting 40% faster quotes/2-point LR to 64%, exited Midwest small auto for E&S up 22%. EMEA 18%, APAC 12% Australia post-floods.

Specialty 16% $2.3 billion up 11.3%: cyber 25.4% $850 million ransomware pricing 20% higher attachments, ML accumulation cut tail 18% for flat reinsurance; marine/energy 9.8% OPEC/Red Sea war exclusions; aviation 4.2% parametric hull.

Life/annuities 10% $1.5 billion up 4.1%: UL 5.2% 4.8% crediting, Japan block $200 million APE; health/supplemental 8.7% $700 million, stop-loss 14% ACA, voluntary on return-to-office, expense 28% on Teladoc.

U.S. 10.5% 65% growth, California/Texas rates despite $120 million hail, 58% attritional LR; Europe 7.2% German D&O; APAC 12.8% India micro 500K policies PhonePe, Australia cyber/flood.

Profitable Growth 2025 targets 8-10% CAGR, mix to 48% commercial/specialty; ApexAI 70% new business +12% wins; embedded API Stripe $150 million; reinsurance cessions -2 points for cyber/climate; IPCC AR6 cat models de-risk $2.5 billion peak.

FY guide 8.5-9.5% GWP no major cats, +5% industry rates; social inflation/cyber risks offset by 250% reserves, $1.2 billion powder.

Investment realized/unrealized gains/losses: $152 billion portfolio—68% fixed 4.2% yield corporates/munis, 18% equities S&P/dividend, 10% alts real estate/infra, 4% cash—book yield 4.1% up 20 bps on repositioning.

Realized net $285 million, +185% YoY/+15% sequential: $180 million financial equities trim JPM/WFC 25% YTD to healthcare/staples 3.2% yield; $120 million intermediate corporates AT&T/Verizon spreads 110 bps to new munis/ABS 4.8%, tax-exempt 22%; losses $15 million bank preferreds. 92% gains/losses vs. peer 75% SNL.

Unrealized net -$420 million, better than Q1 -$750 million/Q2'23 -$1.2 billion, OCI -$3.8 billion (2.5% surplus). Fixed volatility on 4.25% 10-year dip +2% bond return, HY spreads -$280 million; equities +$150 million S&P 5% AI trim tech. U.S. +$90 million munis; Europe -$60 million ECB; EM +$40 million LatAm infra 7.2%.

ALM: duration 5.8 years -$1.2 billion swaps $8 billion notional; derivatives 60% equity vol, VaR 1.8% vs. MetLife 2.2%; $5 billion ESG green/infra +20 bps NAIC climate. H2 realized $200-250 million, unrealized to zero on 50-75 bps cuts/8-10% S&P, 4.3% yield 12% ROE.

Total catastrophe losses $1.45 billion pre-tax, 9.2% GWP, up from Q2 5.8%/Q3'22 6.4%; YTD $3.2 billion 7.1% vs. 6-7% guide midpoint on SCS. Net reinsurance 45% ceded via XoL Swiss Re/Munich/ILW.

U.S. 72% $1.04 billion 12.1% GWP: SCS 18 billion-dollar NOAA, Idalia/Ophelia $450 million, auto hail/wind LR 68% ex-cat, commercial property $320 million; California quiet post-15% non-renewals. Europe 15% $220 million 4.8% Storm Ciarán motor/flood. APAC 10% $145 million 3.9% Typhoon Saola parametric. RoW 3% $45 million.

Ex-cat 92.4% combined, all-in 112.6% below Travelers 115%/Progressive 118%. YTD +28% AM Best $100 billion global, SCS 55% U.S. vs. 35% 2018.

RMS v18.1/AIR climate return periods, CatOptix AI de-risked $2.5 billion GWP 8% U.S. wind; 1Q24 reinsurance 50% flat-3% cheaper, $400 million cat bonds Zenith Re Bermuda; parametric pilots California commercial.

11.4% earned growth >8.2% NAIC, U.S. commercial 12.5% rates; fee consulting +22%. Q4 4-5% GWP, FY 6.8-7.3% $4.1-4.4 billion, 90% ex-cat/12%+ ROE 2024.

Asset allocation: $452 billion invested up 4% YoY, ALM matching 7.2-year duration to 7.5-year liabilities, 520% RBC statutory 92%. Surplus flexible.

Fixed 77% $348 billion yield 4.1% +50 bps Fed 5.25-5.50: 92% IG NAIC 1-2. Govt/agency 22% $77B Treasuries 12%/MBS 10% duration 8.1% 4.3%; IG corporates 38% $132B financials 15%/industrials 12% insurers 4.8% 4.2-year; structured 12% $42B CMBS/ABS 2018+ RMBS $2B 150 bps; munis 5% $17B. Regions: NA 62%, Europe 22% 3.8%, APAC 9% 4.5%, EM 5% 6.2%. BBB trim 15%, $25B swaps hedge annuities $150B +12% YoY.

Equities 13% $59B 6-8% return beta 0.7 yield 2.1%+4%: U.S. large 55% $32B S&P ETFs overweight financials/energy; int'l dev 25% $15B Europe/Japan; EM 20% $12B China/India. +8% YTD vs. S&P 15% defensive 18% tech; $3B futures/options hedge P&C cats, trim 1% high P/E to aristocrats 3.2%.

Alts 10% $45B 9.2% IRR +400 bps publics: PE 40% $18B KKR/Apollo insurance buyouts DPI 1.1x TVPI 1.6x; real assets 30% $13.5B RE Sunbelt/infra Brookfield 6.5% inflation hedge; private credit 20% $9B Ares direct 9-11%; hedge 10% $4.5B Citadel 8%. U.S. 65%/Europe 20%/Asia 15%, +25% commitments $2.5B realizations.

ESG 35% fixed SFDR $10B green; Aladdin scenario +200 bps shocks; alts to 12-15% 2025 $10B private credit like Athene. U.S. liquid, Europe to 25%, India pilots. Risks election/China hedged 15% cash, 3% defaults.

This positions $18-20B NII +15% YoY 7-9% ROE C-1 250% VM-20.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial lines. We are actively managing our exposure to severe convective storms and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-powered portfolio optimization and parametric pricing strategies.

Lisa Chen: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in structured credit and alternatives.

Emily Davis: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times and improved claims resolution rates.

Alex Patel: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new ApexAI underwriting suite is expected to drive significant efficiencies and cost savings.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from James Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

James Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the retention improvements in personal lines amid cat activity?

David Johnson: Good morning, James. As Sarah detailed, our personal auto and homeowners retention hit 87.5% and 92.3%, respectively, through ApexDrive telematics at 42% adoption for personalized UBI discounts reducing lapses 15%, app nudges cutting cancellations 9%, Verisk models non-renewing 7% California high-risk, and 68% bundling adding 250 bps lift. This outpaced peers despite Helene and wildfires.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of higher rates on your investment unrealized losses?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, Maria. Unrealized losses narrowed to $420 million from prior quarters on fixed income duration benefits from the 4.25% 10-year dip and equity offsets from S&P gains, with ALM swaps hedging convexity and derivatives covering 60% equity vol. Our conservative tilt keeps OCI manageable at 2.5% surplus, positioning for convergence on expected cuts.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Hayes with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Hayes: What is the expected impact of IFRS 17 and similar regulatory changes on your actuarial and reinsurance strategy?

Michael Reynolds: Good morning, Robert. Our Bermuda sub is 95% CSM-modeled ahead of IFRS 17, with assumption updates like the $120 million this quarter already incorporating frameworks. Reinsurance diversification and ML PML forecasting support stable ROL into renewals, minimizing impacts while enabling growth in cyber and parametric.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platform?

Alex Patel: Good morning, Lisa. The ApexAI suite and Actuarial Modernization Platform process terabytes of data for 30% better assumption credibility, 40% faster underwriting quotes, 12% higher win rates on 70% new business, and churn prediction catching 65% at-risk policies. This drives 3:1 ROI on $150 million spend, scaling telematics to 50% and embedded insurance for $150 million run-rate.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

David Kim: How are cat losses affecting GWP growth guidance?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, David. At 9.2% Q3 GWP and 7.1% YTD cat load within tolerance, we've held FY 8.5-9.5% on 11.4% earned growth, rate adequacy like 12.5% U.S. commercial, and de-risking via CatOptix trimming 8% wind exposure. Parametric and reinsurance keep ex-cat combined at 92.4%, supporting ROE.

Operator: [Potentially more questions]

David Johnson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
